headline: AWS, Anthropic, OpenAI Race to Hire Deployment Engineers
dek: CNBC and TechRadar report U.S. postings jumped from under 200 in 2023 to over 7,300 in 2026.

s2.label: What happened
s2.title: The race for who deploys AI
body: AWS, Anthropic, OpenAI and Google Cloud are racing for forward deployed engineers, who bring AI inside client companies (CNBC, TechRadar).
According to both outlets, they help customers get past legacy systems and internal barriers.

s3.label: How it works
s3.title: How much each is betting
s3.body: According to CNBC and TechRadar, the amounts vary widely.

points.t: $1 billion for the initiative, starting with hundreds of people (CNBC).
Over $4 billion behind a deployment business (CNBC, TechRadar).
$100 million to train partner companies' engineers (CNBC).

s4.label: Why it matters
s4.title: Jobs and pay surge
body: According to Lightcast, cited by CNBC and TechRadar, U.S. postings rose from under 200 in 2023 to over 7,300 in 2026.
CNBC says the average advertised salary reached $195,456, over three times the median posting in the country.

items.t: TechRadar notes three of the four top hirers are consultancies.
AI firms take on part of making AI work, the outlets say.
CNBC cites uncertainty over the payoff from AI infrastructure spending.

caption.hook: AWS, Anthropic, OpenAI and Google Cloud are racing to hire engineers who deploy AI inside client companies.
body: According to CNBC and TechRadar, AWS committed $1 billion and OpenAI launched a deployment business backed by over $4 billion. Anthropic is investing $100 million to train engineers at partner companies.

Lightcast data shows U.S. postings jumping from under 200 in 2023 to over 7,300 in 2026. CNBC reports the average advertised salary reached $195,456, more than three times the median posting in the country.
caption.cta: Would your company hire an engineer just to deploy AI?
